name: readable-diagrams
description: Editorial diagrams a reader understands on first look: architecture, flow, sequence, timeline, tree, layer stack, bar and quadrant from one JSON spec, plus hover interaction, light/dark skins, CJK-aware typography, and a machine-checked comprehension gate.

interface.shortDescription: Diagrams a reader understands on first look
interface.longDescription:
readable-diagrams turns a system, process or comparison into one self-contained HTML page with an editorial diagram — and then checks that a reader can actually follow it. The page always carries a conclusion-shaped title, a one-line takeaway, a numbered reading path, a legend when it is needed, and a caption that says how to read it. A second gate checks contrast, type floors and connector geometry.

Nine structural types render from one JSON spec: architecture, flow, state, sequence, timeline, tree, layer stack, bar and quadrant. Chart families (line, scatter, sankey, radar, heatmap, Gantt…) are hand-authored against the same page furniture and the same gates. Mermaid, draw.io and Excalidraw imports are redrawn editorially instead of re-rendered. Light and dark skins, CJK-aware typography, hover interaction with no JavaScript, and SVG/PNG export.
defaultPrompt: Draw an architecture diagram of my project.
Turn this Mermaid flowchart into an editorial diagram.
Make a one-page explainer with a diagram.
